newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy discusses immigration, Israel with Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: Italy discusses immigration, Israel with Tunisia.

text.p: Italy has told Tunisia that it wants a bilateral accord on the repatriation of Tunisian illegal immigrants to be concluded as soon as possible, the foreign ministry said on Saturday.
It said in a statement Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini made the call at a "long and cordial" meeting with his Tunisian counterpart, Abderrahim Zouari, late on Friday.
Such an accord was "fundamental for an effective reinforcement of border controls", it said.

Italy, with long coastlines and relatively lax enforcement of deportment orders for illegal immigrants, is a magnet for clandestine entry from North Africa. Many immigrants use the Mediterranean island of Lampedusa as a back-door into Europe.

The statement said the two ministers also discussed the Middle East peace process. "Great concern was expressed over the Israeli decision to move ahead with the construction of the Har Homa settlement", it said.
Israel has enraged Palestinians with its plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim hill in East Jerusalem, known as Har Homa to Israel.

"The demand was expressed for both sides to avoid gestures which could compromise anew the climate of trust labouriously rebuilt after the Hebron deal," the statement said, referring to Israel's agreement to pull back troops from most of the West Bank town.
The ministers also discussed the situation in the Maghreb, relations with Algeria, Libya and the European Union.
